kept_with_reasons.why: the ring must snap into the lower plate (its groove sits below the cable tunnel) and the blade must sit above it; a blade-ring part needs the groove in the upper plate, where it cuts the cable path at 270 deg; print-in-place blade impossible (flat 0.2 mm z gaps)
the latch slides into the bowl before the shell goes on; a plunger on the latch would need a slot from the button bore to the shell rim (pod seal and button O-ring lost)
box prints roof-down and the bowl base-down: the tower would be under the bed; flipping either gives an 82 mm / Ø120 bridge

3_control_panel.location: pod cap (fondello_v63), room side: band centred on the release-button azimuth (button at 76.6 deg from the shaft axis), 182 mm below the shelf; the cap is the dry-box floor, so the band wall IS the dry-box wall: no new joint, no gasket frame

band.shape: straight-ruled band (vertical generatrices between the creases, follows the pod in plan): flatter than the skin, smooth convex creases top and bottom, 6 deg ramps at the ends; regular rectangle in the unrolled view, 23.4 mm tall x ~110 mm long

layout_room_view_left_to_right: LED pair at 51 deg: LED1 status/ON-OFF on top (z -84.0), LED2 Wi-Fi/feedback below (z -93.0)

button_recess.why: a Ø17 bore admits a Ø12-16 fingertip (cylinder, 0.5 mm clearance at Ø16) to the full depth; a paw pad or a snout (spheres Ø25-40) sinks only by its sagitta over the rim (Ø30: 2.6 mm on a flat rim, measured with 15 deg tilted approaches below), so the switch face 8 mm down stays out of reach; the bore drains (axis 3 deg down-outward)

knock_outs.qc_2026_11_10: FLUSH with the band (the first issue had three open Ø17 x 9.5 cups with a 0.8 mm skin: they read as holes, gave claws a hook and were fox-bite weak)
knock_outs.outside: flush; only a 0.3 mm deep engraved ring Ø12 (line 0.6) = the future hole, and a Ø1.2 x 0.3 centre dot = pilot mark; nothing to hook a claw into
knock_outs.skin: the outer wall itself: 2.0 mm (1.7 under the engraving), thinned only from the inside
knock_outs.inside: blind Ø12.4 counterbore whose floor follows the facet (uniform skin), then a flat Ø19 nut-seat face perpendicular to the axis 4.8 mm behind the outer face (the wall is 3.0 mm elsewhere)
drilling_recipe: 1 cap off, dry, on a soft pad, room side up; pick the knock-out (KO1 first)
2 pilot Ø3 mm at the centre dot, square to the band face (it faces 10-14 deg downward; the dot and the Ø12 ring are the marks)
3 step drill (4-12 or 4-20 mm) from the front up to the Ø12 step: one step cuts the 2.0 mm skin and breaks into the Ø12.4 counterbore, so the hole is round and burr-free; low speed, no coolant
4 deburr the inside edge lightly; blow out the chips, check the dry pocket is clean

5 fit a 12 mm IP67 switch (M12 front mount, nut <= 14 AF): front gasket on the outer face, nut on the flat seat; clamp thickness 4.8 mm (check the switch takes it). The outer face is curved in plan (sagitta ~0.4 mm over a Ø15 head): add a thin bead of neutral-cure silicone under the gasket, or

6 if a paw-proof recess is wanted (unit at paw/snout height): glue on a printed bezel ring (Ø17 bore x 8 deep, like the real button) with PETG-compatible adhesive/sealant over the drilled hole; it also gives the gasket a flat seat
7 harness: the spare JST position (KO1) goes to GPIO13 (proposal)

future_switch_fit.envelope: thread Ø12 through the wall, nut 16.2 across corners swinging with 0.3 clearance x 2.5 on the seat, body Ø13 x 11.5 behind the nut

knock_outs.ip: the dry box stays sealed until a knock-out is drilled

light_windows.type: Ø5 clear PC light pipe, flat flush lens, flange Ø8 inside, O-ring 5x1 NBR in a Ø7.2 x 0.75 counterbore (25 % squeeze), retained by its snap barbs or a dab of neutral-cure silicone; LED 3 mm on a 2-wire lead behind it
light_windows.axis: square to the band face (facet normal) since 6.3.0, so the flat lens sits flush all round

measured.v63_first_issue: axes 3 deg down-outward on a face leaning 14-17 deg: lens edge ~0.6-0.7 mm proud / sunk

acoustic_opening.water_trap: none (down-facing holes, nothing above them holds water)

dry_pocket.plan: annular sector behind the band from 44 to 128 deg (section frame; west end 128 since the flush-KO QC so a future KO3 switch body clears it), floor = cap floor, roof 2 mm falling 1 deg westward, opens into the D interior below the cap-lip beam (the lip groove stays continuous on a 2.8 mm beam over the opening)

4_firmware_ui_note.controls: 1 push-button + 2 LEDs + speaker (meaning of the LEDs not final)

mapping.single press: dispense exactly one portion - only while the unit is ON (behaviour contract); while OFF: a short LED blink, no dispense
mapping.double press (2 presses within 400 ms): toggle ON/OFF; switching ON dispenses exactly one portion (contract), switching OFF dispenses nothing
mapping.long press 5 s: reset all settings except Wi-Fi (act on release after the 5 s LED pattern; no dispense)
mapping.long press 10 s: full reset incl. Wi-Fi (act on release after the 10 s LED pattern; no dispense)

rules: a single press is confirmed only after the double-press window (~400 ms) has expired: one press = one cycle, never two
holding the button never repeats a cycle
the meow / sound plays at every portion (speaker behind the down-facing grille)

never dispense at power-on: both disc rest positions are closed; store the last rest position in NVS and command exactly it at boot before enabling the servo PWM; a cold start without a stored value goes to 0 deg; the unit boots OFF
debounce 20-30 ms; long-press thresholds counted from the press, LED patterns at 5 s and 10 s so the user knows when to let go
4_firmware_ui_note.pins: proposal only, not electrically verified: button on GPIO27 (old dispense input, active-low with pull-up), LED1 GPIO2, LED2 a free output (e.g. GPIO25), speaker PWM GPIO26 as today; GPIO13 (old ON/OFF input) freed for KO1

gate_hold.assumptions: full 200 L drum (Ø585 x 850 mm kibble), bulk density 0.45, wall friction 0.3 (kibble on HDPE), Janssen K 0.4; design pressure = max(2 x Janssen at the bottom, Janssen asymptote, hydrostatic without wall friction)
gate_hold.blade_model: PETG plate 3.0 mm, simply supported over the largest inscribed circle of the opening (Ø44.0); the blade rests on the lower plate all round the pie (and on the landing floor past the far edge at full stroke)
gate_hold.creep: long-term stress < 1 MPa: no creep concern
gate_hold.closing: single-bevel knife leading edge (0.6 edge, 25 deg) lifts pieces into the column; over-travel 12.4 deg past the far edge into a landing whose far end has a 1.6 mm drain slot (crumbs fall out, no crumb cake); torque at the ring ~0.1-0.5 N m

drainage.light_pipes: flush with the band face, axes on the facet normal (15-17 deg down-outward)

open_risks: panel switch: the free depth behind the mount wall is 14 mm (servo at 1.7 mm): pick a short-body IP67 type and check its datasheet
fox canine on a flush knock-out: punching SF 1.88 on the 2.0 mm skin, 1.6 on the engraved line (250 N assumed)

a future knock-out switch needs a 12 mm IP67 type with a nut <= 14 AF and <= 14 mm behind the seat; the curved outer face needs silicone under the gasket or a printed bezel (drilling recipe in 3_control_panel.knock_outs)
PT screws in printed PETG: pull-out estimated, not tested; tighten by hand (0.6 N m), at most ~5 re-assemblies per hole
cap service now needs a T10 driver (was tool-free) and releases the panel harness: unplug before pulling the cap off
cable proud 0.4 mm of the shelf face: on a very hard shelf the flange may stand 0.4 mm off the wood at the rim until the jacket yields
A column sits 1.75 mm from the board back: keep the perfboard back free of leads in y 26..34 (as y -5..7 for the C column)
stack screws: P3 key now OK long key (the A column is near the hand envelope)
unit height below the shelf 182.1 (as v6.2)
